name: Establish Therapeutic Alliance
description: Build rapport, trust, and a collaborative partnership to underpin all therapy phases.

goal.objective: Form a secure, empathetic, and collaborative foundation for therapeutic work.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels understood, trusts the therapist, and is actively engaged in session.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient expresses moderate trust and engagement, but relationship feels tentative.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient feels disconnected, mistrustful, or unengaged, impeding therapy progress.

goal.reward_hint: Patient actively participates, communicates openly, and expresses feeling understood.

micro_actions.name: Make Empathic Statements
micro_actions.description: Therapist expresses understanding and validation of patient's feelings through warm, genuine language and welcoming body posture.
states: Any sign of relational strain during session

micro_actions.name: Show Warmth and Genuine Interest
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses attentive tone and open-ended questions to convey authentic concern for the patient's experiences.

micro_actions.name: Collaborative Decision-Making
micro_actions.description: Invite patient input before any session adjustment (e.g., agenda amendments, family involvement), reinforcing equality.
states: When session plans are being revised

micro_actions.name: Greet and Acknowledge Patient Arrival
micro_actions.description: Begin each session with a friendly greeting and brief personal connection to set a trusting tone.

micro_actions.name: Directly Elicit Feedback
micro_actions.description: Therapist invites honest feedback about session quality, therapy progress, and personal reactions.

name: Conduct Cognitive Case Conceptualization
description: Formulate and collaboratively refine an individualized cognitive conceptualization of the patient’s problems.

goal.objective: Achieve a shared cognitive understanding of the patient’s issues to guide treatment.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient have a clear, agreed-upon cognitive case formulation that guides interventions.
success_levels.acceptable: Case conceptualization is mostly clear but may need refinement; both parties broadly agree.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Case conceptualization is unclear, therapist and patient have differing understandings.

goal.reward_hint: Patient can articulate the cognitive model of their problems and connects it to treatment.

states: Presentation of complex or poorly understood problems
Need to target interventions to specific cognitions or beliefs
Periods requiring revision of treatment approach

micro_actions.name: Elicit Patient Narrative and Problem Context
micro_actions.description: Ask open-ended questions for detailed background, current concerns, symptoms, daily routines, and major stressors.

micro_actions.name: Explicitly Check Conceptualization Resonance
micro_actions.description: Present case formulation and invite patient agreement/disagreement, encouraging direct feedback for accuracy.

micro_actions.name: Summarize and Reflect Back
micro_actions.description: Paraphrase patient's story and cognitive patterns aloud in accessible language for confirmation and clarification.

micro_actions.name: Probe for Situational Data and Hypothesis Testing
micro_actions.description: Ask for specific examples that reveal links between situations, thoughts, and mood, and test working hypotheses collaboratively.
states: When constructing or revising cognitive model

name: Psychoeducation and Socialization to Therapy
description: Educate the patient about the cognitive model, therapy structure, session format, and expectations.

goal.objective: Enable patient understanding of CBT principles, methods, and session norms.

success_levels.ideal: Patient understands key CBT concepts and participates actively according to session structure.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient shows basic comprehension but occasional confusion about therapy methods.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unclear about CBT rationale, leading to disengagement or misunderstanding.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates understanding and adherence to session routines and therapeutic rationale.

states: When patient queries about therapy process
If patient shows confusion about session structure

micro_actions.name: Explain Session Structure and Rationale
micro_actions.description: Give accessible explanations of session elements, agenda, expectations, and the therapist’s role.
states: Prior to new task or technique introduction

micro_actions.name: Provide Rationale for Assessment and Intervention
micro_actions.description: State clear reasons for asking certain questions or suggesting specific exercises to foster buy-in.

micro_actions.name: Normalize Symptoms and Emotional Experiences
micro_actions.description: Reassure the patient that their reactions are common and expected in CBT.
states: On patient disclosure of distress or fears

micro_actions.name: Teach Basic CBT Concepts
micro_actions.description: Use analogies, diagrams, and examples to illustrate key ideas like the cognitive triad or automatic thoughts.

name: Collaborative Agenda Setting and Goal Planning
description: Set session agendas and treatment goals in partnership with the patient.

goal.objective: Establish shared, clear session goals and therapeutic objectives.

success_levels.ideal: Patient and therapist collaboratively set and agree upon clear, attainable session and treatment goals.
success_levels.acceptable: Goals are broadly discussed, but some ambiguity or lack of collaboration exists.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Goals are imposed, unclear, or not discussed; patient feels uninvolved.

goal.reward_hint: Patient takes an active role in selecting agenda items and verbalizes goals/goals prioritization.

states: Patient requests to address specific topics

micro_actions.name: Ask Explicit Agenda-Setting Question
micro_actions.description: Invite the patient to suggest items for the session agenda, prioritize goals, and review previous plans.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Revise Agenda
micro_actions.description: Offer options and negotiate session focus when priorities shift mid-session.

micro_actions.name: Record and Review Goals
micro_actions.description: Write down or paraphrase chosen goals aloud and confirm patient agreement.

name: Assessment and Mood Check
description: Gather mood ratings and biopsychosocial information to inform session focus and priorities.

goal.objective: Acquire current emotional and psychological state to guide intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Accurate information obtained and used to tailor session; patient feels heard.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial assessment completed but may lack depth or specificity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Mood and psychological status not assessed, risking inappropriate focus.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist conducts structured check-in and patient reports mood/emotional state openly.

states: When patient seems emotionally distressed or withdrawn
When shift in mood is observed between sessions

micro_actions.name: Ask Specific Mood Check Question
micro_actions.description: Request patient to rate mood (numerically or descriptively) or use emotion charts at session start or noticeable affect shift.

micro_actions.name: Probe for Emotional and Physiological Correlates
micro_actions.description: Inquire about body sensations, affect shifts, and ask for scaling intensity (e.g., 'How strong was that feeling [0-100%]?'').
states: On reporting difficulty with emotion labeling

micro_actions.name: Review and Reflect Mood Ratings
micro_actions.description: Summarize patient’s stated emotional state and ask how it relates to session topics or recent events.

name: Identification and Evaluation of Automatic Thoughts
description: Guide patient to identify, specify, and assess the validity and impact of automatic thoughts.

goal.objective: Patient reliably identifies automatic thoughts and evaluates their accuracy and effects.

success_levels.ideal: Patient regularly and accurately identifies and evaluates automatic thoughts during and between sessions.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient can identify some thoughts but struggles with regularity or specificity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient unable or unwilling to identify or evaluate automatic thoughts.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates automatic thoughts and actively participates in thought evaluation tasks.

states: In sessions focused on cognitive restructuring
When patient reports strong emotions or problematic situations

micro_actions.name: Ask Targeted Questions to Elicit Automatic Thoughts
micro_actions.description: Pose specific queries such as 'What was going through your mind in that moment?' during discussion of problem events.

micro_actions.name: Reality Test Automatic Thought
micro_actions.description: Use Socratic questioning ('What evidence supports or contradicts this thought?') to collaboratively evaluate its validity.

micro_actions.name: Directly Note Automatic Thoughts in Writing
micro_actions.description: Write down or prompt patient to record thought for evaluation and later review.

micro_actions.name: Collect Contextual Examples and Affective Ratings
micro_actions.description: Ask for situational details and emotional intensity scales (numeric or qualitative) for each thought.

micro_actions.name: Correct or Clarify Emotional-Thought Labeling
micro_actions.description: Gently guide patient to accurately pair emotions with automatic thoughts, using emotion charts if needed.

name: Modification of Intermediate and Core Beliefs
description: Identify, evaluate, and collaboratively modify dysfunctional intermediate and core beliefs.

goal.objective: Reduce the influence of maladaptive core beliefs and strengthen adaptive beliefs.

success_levels.ideal: Patient successfully modifies central negative beliefs and adopts adaptive alternatives.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial modification or awareness of core beliefs; progress is evident but incomplete.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Core beliefs remain unaddressed, unchanged, or worsen.

goal.reward_hint: Patient expresses new perspectives, beliefs, or shows behavioral change based on shifts in core beliefs.

states: After automatic thoughts have been identified and persist
If distress or dysfunction seems rooted in deep-seated beliefs
Later therapy stages targeting underlying schemas

micro_actions.name: Apply Downward Arrow Technique
micro_actions.description: Repeatedly ask 'What does this thought mean to you?' or 'What’s the worst that could happen?' until underlying belief surfaces.

micro_actions.name: Socratic Questioning of Beliefs
micro_actions.description: Probe belief evidence, exceptions, and history with questions like 'What supports or contradicts this belief?'

micro_actions.name: Label Belief as Hypothesis
micro_actions.description: Encourage patient to treat beliefs as 'ideas' for testing and discussion to foster cognitive flexibility.
states: When patient appears stuck or rigid in beliefs

micro_actions.name: Examine Advantages and Disadvantages
micro_actions.description: Facilitate discussion of pros/cons of maintaining certain beliefs.

micro_actions.name: Formulate and Rate Alternative Beliefs
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively develop and refine new beliefs, prompting patient for agreement and belief strength rating.

micro_actions.name: Assign Evidence-Collection Homework
micro_actions.description: Instruct patient to monitor and collect evidence for/against both old and new beliefs between sessions.

name: Skill Acquisition and Behavioral Activation
description: Teach practical coping skills, schedule activities, and plan behavioral experiments to improve functioning.

goal.objective: Equip patient with behavioral and cognitive skills to manage symptoms.

success_levels.ideal: Patient applies targeted coping strategies and behavioral activation techniques with steady improvement.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient tries skills/activities but uses them inconsistently.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient resists skills training or avoids behavioral activation.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes behavioral tasks, demonstrates skill use, and reports improvement in mood/functioning.

states: Sessions focusing on overcoming inactivity or avoidance
When patient struggles with specific behavioral targets
When cognitive interventions alone are insufficient

micro_actions.name: Teach and Model Coping Strategies
micro_actions.description: Provide stepwise instruction and role-play on skills such as relaxation, distraction, assertiveness, and problem-solving.
states: During patient distress or skill deficit

micro_actions.name: Suggest and Schedule Specific Activities
micro_actions.description: Offer concrete, manageable behavioral tasks and collaboratively plan their timing.

micro_actions.name: Initiate and Review Behavioral Experiments
micro_actions.description: Guide patient in designing, carrying out, and reflecting on behavioral experiments to test new strategies or cognitions.
states: When new skills need real-world trial

micro_actions.name: Reinforce and Praise Efforts
micro_actions.description: Acknowledge and positively reinforce any steps taken towards activation or skill use.

micro_actions.name: Offer Forced-Choice for Activity Selection
micro_actions.description: Present curated activity options when patient struggles to generate own ideas, offering gentle guidance.

name: Structured Problem Solving
description: Facilitate analysis, brainstorming, and implementation of solutions to current problems.

goal.objective: Enable patient to resolve present difficulties using a collaborative stepwise approach.

success_levels.ideal: Patient learns and applies structured problem solving independently and effectively.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient engages in some steps, but problem-solving process is incomplete.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains stuck or unable/unwilling to engage in structured problem solving.

goal.reward_hint: Patient actively generates solutions, evaluates options, and follows up on plan.

states: When session agenda involves resolving acute problems
Patient reports feeling overwhelmed, stuck, or indecisive

micro_actions.name: Facilitate Stepwise Problem Definition
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to clearly articulate the specific problem needing resolution and break it into manageable parts.

micro_actions.name: Co-Brainstorm Solutions
micro_actions.description: Jointly generate potential solutions using open-ended probes and encouragement of multiple options.

micro_actions.name: Guide through Pros/Cons Analysis
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to consider advantages and disadvantages of chosen solutions prior to implementation.

micro_actions.name: Instruct and Model Skills via Role Play
micro_actions.description: Demonstrate practical steps (e.g., assertiveness, social scripts) and rehearse with patient using simulated scenarios.
states: When skill or strategy is unfamiliar

name: Homework Assignment and Review
description: Set, adapt, and review homework assignments collaboratively to promote skill generalization and progress between sessions.

goal.objective: Foster patient autonomy and mastery by practicing skills outside of sessions.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes homework consistently, reports insights, and skill gains.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient completes some homework, shows partial engagement.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient disengages from homework or fails to complete assignments.

goal.reward_hint: Patient brings completed work, discusses difficulties or successes, and requests new tasks.

states: End of session as ongoing practice
When consolidation of session learning is needed
As a tool for relapse prevention

micro_actions.name: Jointly Propose and Write Homework Assignment
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively select appropriate homework tasks and record them (written/audio) with rationale and reminders.

micro_actions.name: Review Homework Completion and Obstacles
micro_actions.description: Ask patient about previous homework experience, difficulties faced, and reaffirm value of effort.

micro_actions.name: Covertly Rehearse Homework Steps
micro_actions.description: Invite patient to mentally rehearse homework logistics (timing, steps, anticipated problems) with therapist’s support.

micro_actions.name: Problem-Solve Homework Barriers
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively identify and address logistical, emotional, or cognitive obstacles blocking homework completion.

micro_actions.name: Model Mistake-Normalization and Self-Disclosure
micro_actions.description: Therapist may model mistake admission and normalization to reduce patient shame about incomplete homework.

name: Session Summarization and Feedback Elicitation
description: Summarize session key points and elicit patient feedback to reinforce learning and strengthen therapeutic engagement.

goal.objective: Ensure patient comprehension of session content and foster collaborative evaluation.

success_levels.ideal: Patient summarizes learnings and provides constructive feedback.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient acknowledges summary and provides minimal feedback.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Session ends without summary or feedback, patient is confused or uncertain.

goal.reward_hint: Patient restates session takeaways and expresses satisfaction or clarifies misunderstandings.

states: When patient appears disengaged or needs encouragement

micro_actions.name: Summarize Session Progress Aloud
micro_actions.description: Verbally recapitulate main points, therapeutic progress, agreed goals, and insights from session.

micro_actions.name: Prompt Patient to Summarize Adaptive Responses
micro_actions.description: Request patient to restate or record their own adaptive thoughts and key session learnings.

micro_actions.name: Elicit Explicit Feedback
micro_actions.description: Ask open-ended questions about session helpfulness, understanding, and preferences for future focus.

micro_actions.name: Check for Clarity and Helpfulness of Notes
micro_actions.description: Review patient-generated notes/adaptive responses for clarity and completeness, offering concise rewording.

name: Termination Preparation and Relapse Prevention
description: Prepare patient for therapy ending, teach relapse prevention strategies, review skills, and ensure maintenance of gains.

goal.objective: Equip patient for lasting self-management, resilience to setbacks, and successful transfer of skills beyond therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels prepared for ending therapy, has clear relapse prevention plan, and maintains gains.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient feels somewhat prepared; relapse plan and skills review are incomplete.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient feels unprepared or anxious, lacking necessary skills/support for termination.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes readiness for termination and demonstrates relapse prevention strategies.

micro_actions.name: Discuss Course of Recovery and Setbacks Explicitly
micro_actions.description: Talk openly about expected ups and downs, setbacks, plateaus, and normalize these experiences.

micro_actions.name: Coach Use of Relapse Prevention Tools
micro_actions.description: Teach coping cards, thought records, and action planning in preparation for setbacks or periods of distress.

micro_actions.name: Assign and Review Relapse Prevention Homework
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to practice skill use (e.g., coping tools, contacting support, writing skill synopses) and debrief experiences in session.

micro_actions.name: Reframe Setbacks and Explore Automatic Thoughts
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively identify thoughts/beliefs about setbacks, use guided discovery/Socratic questioning to reinforce advantages of skill use and session tapering.

micro_actions.name: Review Skills Learned and Self-Therapy Program
micro_actions.description: Summarize key skills, monitor ongoing progress, and update self-therapy plan in final sessions.
